name: Saccharine Trust
label: SST
lede: A poet who preached from the mic and a guitarist who called himself a non-musician, playing jazz-wrecked punk in Minutemen country, a band SST itself treated as the odd one out and Kurt Cobain filed among his favorite records.

eras.title: Downstairs from D. Boon
eras.text: Jack Brewer and Joe Baiza met in Wilmington looking for summer jobs and built a band out of Brewer's new wave group. Baiza lived downstairs from the Minutemen's D. Boon in San Pedro, and the two bands grew up side by side.

years.h: Jack Brewer and Joe Baiza turn the Obstacles into Saccharine Trust
years.p: [[Joe Baiza|4dfac6b9-47a7-4521-9a3d-32b0740e61d3]] joins [[Jack Brewer|fc657c24-ac50-42d7-b976-f2d9b3675749]]'s new wave band the Obstacles on bass and steers it toward punk. When the others drift away, the two keep going, naming the band after a line in David Bowie's The Bewlay Brothers.
years.xp:
The lineup took almost a year to settle. According to Wikipedia, one of the people who auditioned and didn't get the job was [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]].

Baiza lived downstairs from [[D. Boon|ae1757eb-8679-4cb3-8d3a-33160c953505]] and heard the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] working out their sound before they had a name. Boon came down and introduced himself after hearing Saccharine Trust practice.

years.h: First show: opening with the Minutemen
years.p: Saccharine Trust's first gig is with the Minutemen, then about six months old. The first lineup: Jack Brewer, Joe Baiza on guitar, Luis Maldonado on bass and Richie Wilder on drums.
years.xp: Baiza puts the show in 1979; Wikipedia says 1980. Wilder soon left for Mood of Defiance and Rob Holzman took over the drums. Maldonado wanted straight hardcore, not the jazz the band was drifting toward, and Earl Liberty replaced him.

years.h: On Cracks in the Sidewalk, New Alliance's first comp
years.p: Saccharine Trust record at [[Spot|d95a08a1-80f5-4232-bdb7-4777c369f0f9]]'s studio in Hermosa Beach for Mike Watt's compilation Cracks in the Sidewalk on New Alliance Records.
years.xp: Baiza drew artwork for the comp, and Watt turned it down. Baiza used it on Paganicons instead.

years.h: Black Flag's Greg Ginn signs Saccharine Trust after a San Pedro show
years.p: [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] invite Saccharine Trust to open at the Star Theater in San Pedro. Afterwards [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]] and [[Chuck Dukowski|19a07153-933f-4725-a5de-477cb3554517]] surprise them by asking them to record for SST.

years.h: Paganicons · SST 006
years.p: Recorded in April 1981 at Media Art in Hermosa Beach with Spot and Mike Watt. Eight songs, from the 36-second Mad at the Co. to the five-minute A Human Certainty.
years.xp:
The lineup was Jack Brewer, Joe Baiza, Earl Liberty and Rob Holzman, who then left for Slovenly. Brewer is credited as Joaquin Milhouse Brewer.

AllMusic's John Dougan found Brewer pretentious but singled out Baiza's abrasive guitar.

eras.title: Sermons and free jazz
eras.text: With Tony Cicero on drums and Baiza deep into jazz, Saccharine Trust stopped sounding like anything else on SST. Brewer's biblical sermons, a live album made up on the spot, and Mike Watt at the controls took them as far from hardcore as a punk label could go.

years.h: Surviving You, Always cut at Total Access
years.p: Jack Brewer and Joe Baiza record their first LP in Redondo Beach with Spot and a new rhythm section: Tony Cicero on drums and Mark Hodson on bass.

years.h: Surviving You, Always: Brewer credits himself with sermons
years.p: Biblical imagery, a cornet on Yhwh on Acid and a cover of the Doors' Peace Frog. The cover uses Robert Wiles' photo of Evelyn McHale, who jumped from the Empire State Building in 1947.
years.xp: Brewer's liner-note credit reads vocals and sermons; Wikipedia notes his interest in the TV minister Gene Scott. Baiza was exploring jazz, and it shows.

years.h: Jack Brewer writes God Bows to Math for the Minutemen
years.p: Jack Brewer writes the words to God Bows to Math on the Minutemen's Double Nickels on the Dime. The two bands were constant SST billmates.

years.cap: Worldbroken, SST 046, cover art by Joe Carducci
q: four tuxedoed gents bravely fighting the incessant urge-to-riff
years.h: Worldbroken: a totally improvised show at McCabe's
years.p: At McCabe's Guitar Shop in Santa Monica, Saccharine Trust improvise an entire set behind Jack Brewer's poems, with Mike Watt on bass after Mark Hodson's exit. SST releases the tape as an album.
years.xp:
SST's [[Joe Carducci|6f08ef70-2da6-4575-8ec2-22438145f5d2]] suggested bringing in Watt, and drew the cover. Byron Coley described the band as tuxedoed gents fighting the urge to riff.

It later shaped the Unknown Instructors, and bassist Damon Smith said it changed how he heard punk, jazz and free playing.

years.h: We Became Snakes, produced by Mike Watt
years.p: Saccharine Trust grow to a five-piece with saxophone and a new bassist. It's their last studio album for fifteen years.

years.h: Saccharine Trust break up
years.p: Around 1986 the band stops. SST puts out the compilation The Sacramental Element the same year, and Joe Baiza goes on to the jazz-punk band [[Universal Congress Of|d0478192-4d5a-4180-a627-da061ba22a66]].

eras.title: Tapes, covers, a comeback
eras.text: While the band was gone, SST kept the name alive with a live archive and Sonic Youth covered its most famous song. In the mid-1990s Brewer and Baiza came back with a new rhythm section that Baiza calls the best the band ever had.

years.h: Sonic Youth cover I Am Right
years.p: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] record the Paganicons song I Am Right for SST's compilation The Melting Plot.

years.h: Past Lives: 75 minutes from seven years of live tapes
years.p: SST's live collection runs from shamanic jams to quiet improvisation, recorded well and badly across the band's whole run.

years.h: The Jack Brewer Band on New Alliance
years.p: Jack Brewer's new group releases Rockin' Ethereal on New Alliance. He later records with the jazz trio Bazooka and publishes Rhythm or Suicide, a book of poems and writings.

years.h: Saccharine Trust reunite after a decade
years.p: Jack Brewer and Joe Baiza bring the band back with drummer Brian Christopherson and, by 1997, bassist Chris Stein. They play up and down the West Coast.

years.h: The Great One Is Dead, 15 years after the last one
years.p: The reunited lineup's album comes out on Hazelwood. Recess Records reissues it as a double LP in 2017.

eras.title: Cobain's list, Ginn's vault
eras.text: Saccharine Trust's reputation grew after the fact, helped by Kurt Cobain's journals and a new generation of free-jazz punks. The early records, though, stayed locked at SST.

years.h: Paganicons turns up in Kurt Cobain's top 50
years.p: The published Journals of [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] include Paganicons in his list of favorite records. OC Weekly places it ninth.

years.h: Unknown Instructors: Brewer and Baiza with Watt and Hurley
years.p: Jack Brewer and Joe Baiza join Mike Watt and [[George Hurley|e3644b83-1c19-41fa-bf81-483551cd1588]] of the Minutemen in the [[Unknown Instructors|cfe83568-29ab-4b70-b407-6fabde387a19]] on The Way Things Work, a project built on the Worldbroken idea.

q: Greg Ginn at SST still won't allow anything to be done with it.
years.h: Joe Baiza: Greg Ginn is sitting on Saccharine Trust's records
years.p: Joe Baiza tells Vice that SST's Greg Ginn won't allow anything to be done with the band's catalog, and calls Saccharine Trust the black sheep of the SST roster.
years.xp: In the same interview Baiza says the Minutemen taught him that in a band you have to really put out, and that he still doesn't think of himself as a guitar player.

years.h: Bassist Chris Stein dies of cancer at 44
years.p: Chris Stein, Saccharine Trust's bassist since 1997, dies after cancer spread through his body and twice returned in his brain, OC Weekly reported.
years.xp: Stein also played in Citizen Down with Jason Cruz before [[Strung Out|0220a594-56a1-47ca-8288-001ead3a3546]], and later in Jason Cruz and Howl. He reworked the bass lines in I Am Right in a way that impressed even the band's original bassist.
